opportunities.title: Add unit-tests for all the Gambit predefined procedures
opportunities.summary: This issue has a bounty of $100 CAD. Many of the Gambit predefined procedures have extensive unit tests in the `tests/unit-tests` directory. For example each file in the `tests/unit-tests/04-list` directory contains unit tests for a specific list processing procedure or set of related procedures, and `tests/unit-tests/09-io` is for I/O related procedures. These don't cover all the predefined procedures. For example `tests/unit-tests/09-io` does not contain unit tests for `print`, `println` and `read-line` (which are rather useful and frequently used predefined procedures). There needs to be a way to list all the predefined procedures that are tested by the unit tests so that this list can be compared with `lib/gambit/gambit.sld` which has a list of all the procedures exported by Gambit (that are not in the `##` namespace). This could be done by extending the definitions of the unit testing macros in `tests/unit-tests/#.scm` which are used by all the unit tests. Unit tests need to be added for each predefined procedure not yet tested.

When a complex piece of content is flagged, push it to a secure "Jury Queue". 2. Randomly select 5 highly-rated, active users (with zero prior infractions). 3. If a 4-out-of-5 consensus is reached, automatically execute the deletion or dismissal. 6. Reward the jurors with 50 Gamification points for providing free labor to keep the community clean. ### Expected Effort Hard (Consensus algorithms + Blind voting state machines + RBAC workflows).

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
